newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Rowdy protest greets launch of race row MP's party.
newsitem.headline: Rowdy protest greets launch of race row MP's party.

text.p: Angry protesters waving placards and jostling guests on Friday disrupted the launch of a new political party by maverick politician Pauline Hanson, who caused Australia's bitter race debate last year.
A group of about 50 protesters gathered outside the launch of the "Pauline Hanson's One Nation" party in Ipswich, 30 kms (18 miles) east of Brisbane.
Hanson, a former fish and chip shop owner who is an independent MP from Queensland state, created an international storm last year with her attacks on Asian immigration and Aboriginal welfare.
She announced her intention last month to launch a new party and become a major force in politics.
Protesters outside her party launch held placards which read "Pauline Hanson has to go", "Kick out the racists" and "The fish and chips bitch from Ipswich".
A window was broken when protesters began banging on a plate-glass door after one of Hanson's supporters opened a side entrance to the Ipswich City Hall to let guests in.
Guests were then escorted into the hall through a police cordon. A spokesman for Ipswich police said no arrests were made and no one was injured.
Hanson made headlines in Australia and beyond last September with her maiden speech in parliament which warned that the country was "in danger of being swamped by Asians".
She had not arrived when the protests began and was due to speak later on Friday night.
